samples.summary: `SELF_CLOSE_RE` strips a trailing `/` that belongs to an unquoted attribute value, silently corrupting the value
samples.evidence: `const region = (match[1] ?? '').replace(SELF_CLOSE_RE, '')` (line 175) runs `/\/\s*$/` over the whole attribute region *before* attributes are parsed, so it cannot tell a self-closing slash from the last character of an unquoted value. For `` the region does not end in `/`, so that case is fine — but `` yields region ` width=1 src=https://example.com/photos/ `, whose trailing `/ ` is stripped, producing `src="https://example.com/photos"` — a different URL than the author wrote (a directory-index src becomes a path with no trailing slash, which many servers 404 or redirect). Same for `` → `alt="x"`. Quoted values are unaffected. The parse would be unambiguous if the slash were removed after attribute tokenisation (i.e. only when it is not part of a matched value), rather than by a regex on the raw region.

samples.summary: Module-level `g`/`y` regexes carry `lastIndex` across calls; correctness depends on every future caller remembering to reset it
samples.evidence: `ATTR_RE` (global) and `IMG_TAG_RE` (sticky) are module singletons whose `lastIndex` is mutable state. Both current uses do reset it (`ATTR_RE.lastIndex = 0` at img-plugin.ts:98, `IMG_TAG_RE.lastIndex = state.pos` at :168), so there is no bug today, but `parseAttrs` returns early on several paths leaving `ATTR_RE.lastIndex` non-zero, so any new call site that forgets the reset silently mis-parses rather than failing loudly. Not reachable now — flagged as a latent hazard only.
